# Short-term rental regulation

Whether and where a property may legally be let on Airbnb-style terms, split
prime-city vs elsewhere. Sources in [citations.md](../citations.md).

**The distinction that governs this file: in force, versus announced.** For
every restriction below, the status is stated. A municipal press release
announcing a future ban is not an enacted instrument, and a research brief that
loses that distinction produces fabricated effective dates.

## Summary

| Country | Registration | Prime-city restriction | Status |
|---|---|---|---|
| Spain | National registry **annulled** by the Supreme Court; licensing is regional/municipal | Barcelona: all ~10,000 HUT licences to lapse by Nov 2028 | Registry enacted then annulled [15][16]; Barcelona announced under an enacted Catalan decree-law [17][18] |
| Greece | National registry (AADE) | **Athens districts 1–3: first registration banned to 31.12.2026**; Thessaloniki A' from 1.7.2026 | In force by statute + ΚΥΑ [25] |
| Portugal | National (RNAL) | Municipal opposition window, extended in *áreas de contenção* | In force [19][20]; the 2023 national freeze was **repealed** [21] |

| France | Municipal | Paris: **90 nights/year** for a principal residence; change-of-use with compensation otherwise | In force [24] |
| Hungary | National NTAK, preceded by a notary operating licence | None found | In force, no date evidenced [26] |

## Spain — the national registry was created, then struck down

Real Decreto 1312/2024 created a single rental registry and a digital single
window, implementing Regulation (EU) 2024/1028. Its entry-into-force clause,
quoted verbatim from the BOE [15]:

> "El presente real decreto entrará en vigor el día 2 de enero de 2025,
> desplegando efectos sus disposiciones el 1 de julio de 2025…"

Note an internal inconsistency in the same document: the BOE's own ANÁLISIS
metadata block says "Efectos desde el 1 de junio de 2025" — June, against July in
the operative clause. The operative clause governs.

**Then the Supreme Court annulled the core of it.** The consolidated text, last
updated 18 July 2026 [16], marks arts. 5, 8, 9, 10, 2(f), 2(i), 12(b), 12(c) and
the second additional provision as "(Anulado)", with arts. 1, 2(j), 6 and the
first final provision partly annulled. The annulling judgments are **TS 19 May
2026 (BOE-A-2026-12300), 21 May 2026 (BOE-A-2026-13893) and 1 June 2026
(BOE-A-2026-15677)**, plus a catch-all annulling any other single-registry
provision.

What survives: art. 7, the Ventanilla Única Digital. What does not: the
registration-number mechanism itself — the obligation whose absence stopped a
property being listed.

An investor who complied in 2025 complied with a regulation now substantially
void, and the ministry's own guidance pages on the current position are
inaccessible to this run [69]. **What replaces it is not established here.**

Licensing was never national in any case: RD 1312/2024 expressly disclaims
competence over "procedimientos de autorización o licencia" exercised by other
administrations on tourism or housing grounds [15].

### Barcelona

The city page states the outcome plainly [17]: "A Barcelona, el 2028,
s'eliminaran les llicències d'habitatges d'ús turístic", recovering 10,000
dwellings. A legal *habitatge d'ús turístic* is a whole dwelling let for stays of
31 days or fewer, requiring a municipal licence and a Catalan registry number.

The instrument matters. The city is **applying an existing Catalan decree-law**,
not enacting a new ban [18]: "el Ayuntamiento de Barcelona se acoge a lo
establecido por el decreto-ley 3/2023 de noviembre, que determina que la
vigencia de las licencias actuales terminará en un plazo de cuatro años y no se
emitirán nuevas licencias." The deputy mayor confirms the future PEUAT will
contain no HUT category, so "no existirá la licencia para este tipo de
alojamiento".

Classification: the **four-year licence sunset is an enacted Catalan
decree-law**; the **PEUAT category removal is announced municipal policy**. The
decree-law text itself was not retrieved, so this is the city's characterisation
of it. Enforcement runs at an average 300 complaints per month [18].

## Greece — a freeze that a purchase itself triggers

The Ministry of Social Cohesion and Family page [25] gives the full legal chain:
under para. 2A of art. 111 of Law 4446/2016, added by art. 29 of Law 5162/2024
and shaped by art. 5 of Law 5313/2026, **first-time registration** in the
Short-Term Residence Property Registry is prohibited for property in the **1st,
2nd and 3rd Municipal Districts of Athens**. Originally to 31.12.2025, extended
to **31.12.2026** by ΚΥΑ 225563 ΕΞ 2025/2025 (ΦΕΚ Β΄ 7200/31.12.2025). The same
restriction applies to the **1st Municipal Community of Thessaloniki from 1 July
2026 to 31 December 2026**.

Penalties: an administrative fine of **50% of the income earned, minimum
€20,000**; on a repeat breach in the same tax year, **the whole of rents
received, minimum €40,000**.

The clause that matters most to a buyer:

> "Ακίνητα εντός των παραπάνω περιοχών που μεταβιβάζονται εν ζωή, για
> οποιαδήποτε αιτία (επαχθή ή χαριστική), διαγράφονται από το Μητρώο Ακινήτων
> Βραχυχρόνιας Διαμονής και δεν είναι δυνατή η επανεγγραφή τους όσο διαρκεί ο
> περιορισμός."

Property in those districts transferred inter vivos, for any cause, is **deleted
from the registry, and cannot be re-registered while the restriction lasts**.
Buying a running short-let in central Athens extinguishes its registration. Any
valuation that assumes the seller's registry status passes with the property is
wrong.

The restriction may be extended further "με κανονιστική διοικητική πράξη" — by
administrative act, without new legislation.

**Everything else about the Greek regime is unavailable.** The AADE registration
rules, the AMA number and the day thresholds are all behind sources that refuse
this run's fetch service [64].

## Portugal — the 2023 freeze was repealed

Registration is national, through the Balcão Único Eletrónico, with the registry
number issued after **60 working days**, or **90 working days** in *áreas de
contenção*, absent municipal opposition [19]. Note a direct conflict between two
official government sources: gov.pt states the same periods as 60 and 90 **days**
without "úteis" [20]. Both are government publishers; neither is obviously
superior.

**The Mais Habitação restrictions are gone.** The consolidated text of Lei
56/2023 [21] marks as revoked by DL 76/2024: art. 19.º (suspension of new AL
registrations), art. 20.º (re-examination of issued registrations), art. 21.º
(lapse of inactive registrations) and art. 52.º; and art. 22.º, the extraordinary
AL levy (CEAL), as revoked by DL 57/2024. So the nationwide registration freeze,
the periodic licence re-review and the AL levy have all been withdrawn.

**What survives is private-law, and it bites.** Art. 17.º of Lei 56/2023 [21]
amended the base regime so that registration in a fraction designated for
housing "deve o registo ser precedido de decisão do condomínio"; a condominium
assembly may oppose AL activity by a deliberation of at least **two-thirds of the
building's permilage**, with cancellation of the registration determining
immediate cessation; and the registration number is "pessoal e intransmissível",
with transfer of **any** share of a corporate holder's capital triggering the
same consequence.

The practical reading: Portugal removed the national freeze but left the
building's other owners holding a veto, and made the licence non-transferable.

**Caveat on source quality.** The official gazette copies both failed [11], so
the repeal detail rests on a non-official consolidator.

## Italy — three stacked layers, in force since 2 November 2024

The commencement is precisely evidenced [23]: art. 13-ter of DL 145/2023,
converted by Law 191 of 15 December 2023, created the CIN; Ministry Decree Prot.
16726 of 6 June 2024 set the interoperability rules; the BDSR entry into
operation was published in *Gazzetta Ufficiale* Parte Seconda n. 130 of **3
September 2024**, and under comma 15 the regime applies from the sixtieth day
after — **2 November 2024**. The ministry FAQ confirms it and adds that
**sanctions apply from 2 January 2025** [22].

Three layers, all mandatory [22][23]: municipal SCIA or CIA; regional
registration and code; national CIN. "Il CIN non sostituisce il codice
identificativo regionale/provinciale" — both must be displayed.

Penalties under comma 9 [22]: absence of CIN €800–€8,000; failure to display
€500–€5,000 per unit plus immediate removal of the listing; missing gas and CO
detectors and compliant extinguishers €600–€6,000 per violation, applying to
non-entrepreneurial lettings too; entrepreneurial letting without SCIA
€2,000–€10,000.

**The volume ceiling changed in 2026** [28]: the short-let tax regime applies
only where **no more than two apartments** are so used in a tax period, against
four until 31 December 2025. Beyond that the activity "si presume svolta in forma
imprenditoriale", which drags in the SCIA and plant-safety obligations. A
three-unit portfolio assembled under the old rule is reclassified by operation
of law.

No Italian night cap, licence cap or city zoning ban appears in any fetched
source.

## France — Paris is 90 nights, not 120

The Ville de Paris page states it twice [24]: "la limite est de **90 jours par
an**", with a penalty of up to €10,000 per year of overrun. **This corrects the
120-night figure carried in the research brief** — no fetched source supports
120, and the national default was not established.

Two tracks [24]:

- **Principal residence** (occupied ≥8 months/year): online declaration,
  immediate registration number that must appear on every listing, taxe de
  séjour, 90-day cap.
- **Anything else** — which is by definition a non-resident investor's position:
  an *autorisation de changement d'usage* **with compensation**, meaning
  "transformer en logement des locaux non dédiés à l'habitation (bureau,
  commerce…)"; plus a *changement de destination* to hotel use; plus
  registration; plus taxe de séjour. "Ces autorisations sont nécessaires dès le
  1er jour de location."

That compensation requirement is a capital barrier, not a form. Penalties reach
**€100,000** plus an astreinte of up to €1,000 per day per m², and false
declaration carries up to one year imprisonment and €80,000 [24]. Social housing
is prohibited outright.

**Condominium rule in force since 21 November 2024** [24]: all new co-ownership
rules must state whether tourist letting is permitted, and existing rules may be
amended to prohibit it for anything other than a principal residence — available
only where the rules already bar commercial activity in dwellings.

No source covers any French city other than Paris.

## Hungary, Costa Rica

**Hungary** [26]: all accommodation establishments must register in NTAK and
supply data daily; a **notary-issued operating licence is a prerequisite
document**, so the municipal layer sits upstream of the national one. The page
carries no dates, statute numbers, caps or zoning provisions, and no fetched
source covers Budapest district-level restrictions. Do not assert one.

**Costa Rica** [27]: national ICT registration for hosts and platform
intermediaries under arts. 10 and 11 of Ley N° 9742 of 29 October 2019; ICT
validates within 15 natural days and publishes within 5 working days; failure to
register means "funcionamiento ilegal" under art. 14. No cap, night limit or
zoning rule appears.

## Mexico and Panama — nothing

**Mexico**: all five Mexico City sources timed out [67]. Note that three of the
five were titled as a *proposal* or an *announcement* rather than an enacted
instrument — precisely the source shape that produces fabricated effective dates
when a snippet is treated as evidence. No claim about Mexican short-term rental
regulation is made in this document.

**Panama**: the Gaceta Oficial copies of Ley 122 de 2019 failed on DNS, PDF
parse and 404; a fourth copy returned HTTP 200 but extracted only running
headers, indicating a scanned image PDF with no text layer [68]. Panama's
short-stay lodging restriction cannot be stated, dated, or characterised as in
force from this run.

## Gaps and limitations

- Mexico and Panama: no source at all.
- Greece: everything except the moratorium.
- Spain: what replaces the annulled registry; the three TS judgments themselves.
- France: everything outside Paris, and the national night-cap default.
- Hungary: statute numbers, dates, and any district-level rule.
- Italy: any municipal restriction, in any city.
- Portugal: which municipalities have declared *áreas de contenção*.
